text: Define cloud and on-prem infrastructure in human-readable config files that can be versioned, reused, and shared
quote: HashiCorp Terraform is an infrastructure as code tool that lets you define both cloud and on-prem resources in human-readable configuration files that you can version, reuse, and share.

text: Generate an execution plan that previews resource creates, updates, and destroys before applying
quote: creates an execution plan, which lets you preview the changes that Terraform plans to make to your infrastructure

text: Skip interactive approval and auto-approve a plan when applying
quote: -auto-approve - Skips interactive approval of the plan before applying

text: Output a JSON representation of the plan, configuration, and state via terraform show -json
quote: terraform show -json shows a JSON representation of the plan, configuration, and current state

text: Import existing cloud resources into Terraform state from the CLI
quote: You can import an existing resource to state from the Terraform CLI.

text: Use the terraform state CLI command to inspect and modify state
quote: Terraform provides the terraform state command to perform basic modifications of the state using the CLI.

text: Run tests that validate module changes against short-lived resources without risking real infrastructure
quote: Terraform tests let authors validate that module configuration updates do not introduce breaking changes. Tests run against test-specific, short-lived resources, preventing any risk to your existing infrastructure or state.

text: Emit a stream of JSON UI messages for long-running commands like plan, apply, refresh, and test
quote: For long-running commands such as `plan`, `apply`, `refresh`, and `test`, the `-json` flag outputs a stream of JSON UI messages.

text: Define policy-as-code rules that validate plans against security and compliance requirements
quote: Policies are rules for Terraform runs that let you validate that Terraform plans comply with security rules and best practices.

text: Provide an MCP server giving AI models real-time access to provider docs, modules, and policies
quote: The Terraform Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enhances AI models with real-time access to current Terraform provider documentation, modules, and policies from the Terraform registry.

text: Publish and consume providers, modules, and policies via a public registry
quote: Anyone can publish and consume providers, modules, and policies on the public Terraform Registry.

text: Automate infrastructure provisioning across any cloud provider
quote: Automate Infrastructure on Any Cloud

text: Create reusable infrastructure configurations packaged as modules
quote: Create reusable configurations with modules.

text: Build a dependency graph of resources and parallelize creation/modification of non-dependent resources
quote: Terraform builds a graph of all your resources, and parallelizes the creation and modification of any non-dependent resources.

text: Apply command executes a plan, auto-generating one if needed and prompting for approval before performing operations
quote: Terraform automatically creates a new execution plan as if you had run terraform plan, prompts you to approve that plan, and performs the indicated operations.

text: Show command renders human-readable output from a saved state or plan file
quote: The `terraform show` command provides human-readable output from a state or plan file.

text: State file maps real-world resources to configuration, tracks metadata, and improves performance for large infra
quote: Terraform uses your workspace's state to map real world resources to your configuration, keep track of metadata, and to improve performance for large infrastructures.

text: Mock provider-returned data during terraform test runs
quote: Terraform v1.7.0 introduced the ability to mock data returned by the providers during a `terraform test` execution.

text: Write custom providers/plugins to extend supported resources
quote: You can also [write your own](/terraform/plugin).

text: Save a generated plan to a file that can later be applied exactly as previewed
quote: You can use the optional `-out=FILE` option to save the generated plan to a file on disk, which you can later execute by passing the file to `terraform apply`
